question: Which of the following is a festival primarily celebrated in the state of Odisha?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Parba**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Raja Parba** is a three-day festival celebrated in Odisha, India.

• This festival marks the onset of the monsoon and the earth's menstruation period.

• Raja Parba is mainly dedicated to the celebration of womanhood and the menstrual cycle.

• The festival involves various traditional games, folk songs, and special foods prepared for the occasion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Baishagu**

• Baishagu is a festival celebrated by the Bodo community in Assam.

• It is observed during the spring season, especially in the month of April.

• The festival involves traditional dance, music, and feasting.

• **Chhath**

• Chhath is an ancient Hindu Vedic festival dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and his consort Usha.

• It is primarily celebrated in Bihar, Jharkhand, and Uttar Pradesh.

• The festival includes rituals such as fasting, offering prayers to the Sun, and taking holy baths in rivers.

• **Me-Dam-Me-Phi**

• Me-Dam-Me-Phi is a festival celebrated by the Ahom community in Assam.

• It is observed to pay homage to the ancestors and departed souls.

• The festival includes rituals such as offering food and prayers to the ancestors.
